subject: Capacity Rebanding & Annual Renewal — Nonlinear Commit Lift Proposal
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
To: Claire Martin <claire.martin@everlane-retail.com>
Cc: ops@everlane-retail.com
Date: 2027-10-25T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed capacity rebanding for 2028 renewal

Hi Claire,

Thanks again for the candid conversation earlier — really appreciate the transparency on seasonal peaks. Attached is a short proposal that captures a non-linear commit uplift we discussed (rather than a single flat monthly commit). Key points: 

- Start Year 1: 300M tokens/month committed baseline.
- Year 2: 450M tokens/month (automatic roll-up if usage milestones met).
- Year 3: 600M tokens/month.
- Burst pocket: 25M tokens/month for seasonal spikes (billed at overage rate if exceeded).
- Rate bands: stepped unit price that becomes favorable as you cross each band; we can lock pricing for the 3-year term.

We built in a modest ramp so you get predictable SLOs while also reducing unit cost as you scale. I attached a one-page summary and a short technical appendix describing how we will map rate limits and burst behavior (KV cache, prefix caching, and per-route soft-throttle).

If this shape looks directionally right, can we schedule a 30-min procurement + ops call next week to talk payment cadence, invoice schedule, and SSO/SCIM provisioning?

Attachments: [attachment: Everlane_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf (PDF, 284 KB)], [attachment: Everlane_Technical_Appendix.xlsx (XLSX, 112 KB)]

Cheers,
Naomi Feldman
Account Director, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Claire Martin <claire.martin@everlane-retail.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@everlane-retail.com>, ops@everlane-retail.com
Date: 2027-10-26T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed capacity rebanding for 2028 renewal

Hi Naomi,

Thanks — I reviewed the PDF and the ramping approach looks promising. A few quick clarifications from procurement and platform ops before we move to terms: 

1) Procurement: we prefer an annual invoicing cadence; will you accept a 60-day net invoice for the first year and 30-day net thereafter? Also, can you provide a sample SOW/term sheet we can run internally?

2) Ops: the burst pocket mechanics — will bursts be enforced per-route or at account level? We need guarantees that realtime checkout flows never see soft-throttles.

3) Price lock: you mention locking pricing for the 3-year term. Can you confirm that the unit price for tokens in Year 3 will be no higher than Year 1 pricing (i.e., strictly non-increasing)?

Attached: [attachment: Everlane_PO_Intent.pdf (PDF, 42 KB)] — this is our internal PO intent, not a formal PO yet.

Also copying our procurement lead for availability on a call next week.

Best,
Claire Martin
Head of Platform, Everlane Retail
claire.martin@everlane-retail.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Claire Martin <claire.martin@everlane-retail.com>
Date: 2027-10-26T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposed capacity rebanding for 2028 renewal — need pricing/ops answers

Karthik / Hannah — looping you both in. Claire from Everlane backfilled procurement and ops questions after reviewing our draft ramp. High level asks: 60d/30d invoice cadence flexibility, burst enforcement details (per-route vs account), and a confirmation that pricing is non-increasing across the term.

Can we propose a reconciled commercial that: 
- Accepts 60d for Year 1 with an invoice schedule that maps to their fiscal calendar.
- Confirms account-level burst pocket but with route-level exceptions for flagged checkout traffic (we can carve out a small set of route IDs that bypass soft-throttle).
- Publishes an explicit price ladder with maximum unit price capped across all years and a progressive discount as commits scale.

Any quick redlines I should share with Claire before the call? Looking to schedule a 30-minute call Tuesday 11/2.

Thanks,
Naomi

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Claire Martin <claire.martin@everlane-retail.com>
Date: 2027-10-27T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed capacity rebanding for 2028 renewal — need pricing/ops answers

Naomi / Hannah — thanks for the context. My suggested commercial outline to present to Claire: 

- Term: 36 months with annual invoice schedule (we'll support Year-1 60d net as an exception).
- Commit ladder: Yr1 300M tokens/mo, Yr2 450M tokens/mo, Yr3 600M tokens/mo.
- Burst: 25M tokens/mo account-level burst pocket.
- Checkout carve: up to 3 route IDs marked for soft-throttle exclusion — ops to provide list and we'll whitelist on the gateway.
- Pricing: two-tier ladder where effective unit price per 1M tokens decreases at 450M and again at 600M; explicit language: "unit price will not exceed Year-1 unit price at any later point in the term."
- Discount: for committing to the full 36-month ramp we'll offer a blended 18% discount across the term (applied as a credit to invoices).

I'll draft a short term-sheet and sample invoice schedule. Hannah — can you confirm technical feasibility for per-route carve outs and whether SCIM provisioning can be completed within a three-week window post-signature?

Karthik
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
To: Claire Martin <claire.martin@everlane-retail.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@everlane-retail.com>, ops@everlane-retail.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity Rebanding & Annual Renewal — Nonlinear Commit Lift Proposal — next steps

Claire / team — appreciate the time on the call today. Per our discussion, we aligned on the following and I wanted to confirm in writing so procurement has a single list of deliverables: 

1) Commercials: 36-month term with the commit ladder Karthik outlined (300M / 450M / 600M tokens per month). Blended 18% credit across the term applied monthly.
2) Invoicing: Year 1 invoice on a 60-day net schedule as an exception; Years 2–3 on 30-day net.
3) Burst & routing: 25M account-level burst; up to 3 checkout route IDs will be exempt from soft-throttle. Ops to share route IDs by 2027-12-07.
4) Onboarding: SCIM/SSO provision and a dedicated kickoff within three weeks post-signature. Ops to open a ticket referencing SUP-4289.
5) Legal/compliance: we'll produce a short term-sheet and a 1-page SOW. Procurement to return a PO or DocuSign within two weeks to lock the start-of-term.

Next steps: I will upload the term-sheet and DocuSign link this afternoon. Claire — once procurement confirms the PO intent we can cut a DocuSign envelope and start SCIM onboarding immediately.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/ABCDEF-123456
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/EVR-2079

Thanks — looking forward to getting Everlane onboarded for the new ramp.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Director, Redwood Inference
